answer: Require a hardware attestation for every identity that wants to grade. The enclave signs a measurement of the running code, the network checks it against a known-good set, and it expires after one epoch. Tax any attestation that comes from a single subnet, and cap the reward at the summit once a group exceeds ten members. Assume the attacker can rent the same hardware; then the defense is that 1,000 enclaves cost more than 1,000 honest tasks. The zenith of the reward curve must sit below that line, and a pigment tag on clustered attestations marks the groups that hit it.
